items.title: Physics I — Units, Motion, Force & Gravitation
items.body:
## Units & Measurement

- **Seven SI base units**: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (current), **kelvin (temperature)**, mole (amount), candela (luminous intensity).
- **Derived units**: newton (force), joule (energy), watt (power), pascal (pressure), hertz (frequency).

## Motion (Kinematics)

- **Scalars** (magnitude only): distance, speed, mass, energy. **Vectors** (magnitude + direction): displacement, velocity, acceleration, force.
- **Equations of motion**: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as.
- In **uniform circular motion**, speed is constant but velocity changes (direction changes).

## Force & Newton's Laws

| Law | Statement |
|---|---|
| First | A body stays at rest/uniform motion unless acted on by a force (**inertia**) |
| Second | F = ma (= rate of change of momentum) |
| Third | Every action has an equal and opposite reaction (on a **different** body) |

- **Momentum** = mass × velocity; it is conserved in collisions.

## Gravitation

- **Universal law**: F = G·m₁m₂/r².
- **g ≈ 9.8 m/s²**; greater at poles than equator; **g on Moon ≈ g/6**.
- **Mass** is constant everywhere; **weight (W = mg)** varies with g (zero at Earth's centre).
- **Work** W = F·s·cosθ (zero if force ⟂ displacement); **Power** = work/time (watt); **1 HP ≈ 746 W**; energy is conserved.

## Fluids — Pressure & Buoyancy

- **Pressure** P = F/A; in a fluid **P = hρg** (rises with depth); **atmospheric pressure ≈ 101 kPa** at sea level and falls with altitude.
- **Archimedes' principle**: upthrust (buoyant force) = weight of fluid displaced. A body **floats** when its average density < the fluid's; a **hydrometer** and ship flotation use this.
- **Pascal's law**: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally (hydraulic brakes/lift).
keyPoints: Seven SI base units include kelvin (temperature) and mole (amount); newton/joule/watt are derived.
Displacement, velocity and acceleration are vectors; distance and speed are scalars.
Newton's 1st law = inertia; 2nd law F = ma; 3rd law action-reaction act on different bodies.
Momentum = mass × velocity and is conserved in collisions.
g is greater at the poles than the equator and about one-sixth on the Moon; weight = mg, mass is constant.
Work = F·s·cosθ (zero when force is perpendicular to displacement); 1 horsepower ≈ 746 watts.
Archimedes' principle: upthrust = weight of displaced fluid; a body floats if its density < fluid's; pressure P = hρg.
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9 — Motion; Force and Laws of Motion; Gravitation; Work and Energy

items.title: Physics II — Light, Sound & Heat
items.body:
## Light

- **Reflection**: angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
  - **Concave mirror** (converging) → shaving/makeup mirror, vehicle headlights, torches.
  - **Convex mirror** (diverging) → vehicle rear-view mirror (wider field, erect diminished image).
- **Refraction**: bending of light between media; measured by **refractive index**.
  - **Convex lens** = converging (magnifying glass, corrects hypermetropia); **concave lens** = diverging (corrects myopia).
- **Dispersion**: a prism splits white light into **VIBGYOR**; rainbow is dispersion + internal reflection.
- Eye defects: **myopia** (short sight → concave lens), **hypermetropia** (long sight → convex lens), **presbyopia**, **cataract**.

## Sound

- A **mechanical wave** that needs a medium — cannot travel through vacuum.
- Speed: **solids > liquids > gases** (~343 m/s in air at room temperature).
- **Audible range** 20 Hz – 20,000 Hz; **infrasound** < 20 Hz; **ultrasound** > 20,000 Hz.
- **Echo** = reflected sound; **SONAR** uses ultrasound to find sea depth/objects.

## Heat

| Mode | Medium | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Conduction | Solids | Heating a metal rod |
| Convection | Fluids | Sea/land breeze, boiling water |
| Radiation | None (vacuum) | Heat from the Sun |

- **Specific heat**: water's is unusually high (moderates coastal climate).
- **Latent heat**: absorbed/released during a change of state at **constant temperature** (melting, boiling).
keyPoints: Concave mirror converges (headlights, shaving); convex mirror diverges (rear-view, wide view).
Convex lens is converging and corrects hypermetropia; concave lens is diverging and corrects myopia.
A prism disperses white light into VIBGYOR; refraction is the bending of light between media.
Sound needs a medium (no sound in vacuum) and travels fastest in solids; audible range 20 Hz-20 kHz.
Ultrasound (>20 kHz) is used in SONAR to measure sea depth; echo is reflected sound.
Heat transfer: conduction (solids), convection (fluids), radiation (works in vacuum, e.g. the Sun).
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9-10 — Light: Reflection and Refraction; Sound; Heat

items.title: Physics III — Electricity, Magnetism & Modern Physics
items.body:
## Electricity

- **Ohm's law**: V = IR (at constant temperature). Resistance in **ohms (Ω)**.
- **Series circuit**: same current through all; resistances add (R = R₁ + R₂ + …).
- **Parallel circuit**: same voltage across each; household wiring is in parallel.
- **Electric power** P = VI = I²R = V²/R; commercial unit of energy = **kilowatt-hour (unit)**.
- **Fuse/MCB**: connected in **series** in the live wire; melts/trips on overload (heating effect).

## Magnetism & Electromagnetism

- A current-carrying conductor produces a **magnetic field** (Oersted).
- **Electromagnetic induction** (Faraday): a changing magnetic field induces a current → basis of the **generator/dynamo**.
- **Electric motor**: converts electrical energy → mechanical energy.

## Modern Physics

- **Atom** = nucleus (protons + neutrons) with electrons around it.
- **Radioactivity** emissions: **alpha** (helium nucleus), **beta** (electron), **gamma** (EM radiation).
- **Nuclear fission**: heavy nucleus splits → energy (nuclear reactors, atom bomb).
- **Nuclear fusion**: light nuclei combine → energy (**the Sun**, hydrogen bomb; ITER is experimental).
keyPoints: Ohm's law: V = IR; electric power P = VI = I²R; commercial energy unit = kilowatt-hour.
In series the current is the same; household appliances are wired in parallel.
A fuse/MCB is connected in series in the live wire and works on the heating effect of current.
Electromagnetic induction (Faraday) is the basis of the generator; a motor converts electrical to mechanical energy.
Radioactive emissions: alpha (He nucleus), beta (electron), gamma (EM radiation).
Fission (heavy nucleus splits) powers reactors; fusion (light nuclei combine) powers the Sun.
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10 — Electricity; Magnetic Effects of Electric Current; Structure of the Atom

figure.caption: Radio → microwave → infrared → visible → ultraviolet → X-ray → gamma (rising frequency/energy).

items.title: Chemistry I — Matter, Atoms, Acids-Bases & Common Compounds
items.body:
## Matter

- **States**: solid, liquid, gas (plasma, BEC advanced). **Sublimation** = solid → vapour directly (camphor, dry ice).
- **Classification**: element → compound → mixture.

| Type | Example |
|---|---|
| Element | Iron, oxygen, gold |
| Compound | Water, CO₂, common salt |
| Mixture | Air, sea water, soil |

- **Physical change** → no new substance (melting ice); **chemical change** → new substance (rusting, burning).

## Atomic Structure

- **Atomic number (Z)** = protons; **Mass number (A)** = protons + neutrons.
- **Isotopes**: same Z, different A (C-12/C-14; protium/deuterium/tritium).
- **Valency** = combining capacity (carbon = 4 → CH₄).

## Acids, Bases & Salts

- **pH scale 0–14**: < 7 acidic, 7 neutral, > 7 basic. Indicators: litmus, phenolphthalein, methyl orange.
- **Neutralisation**: acid + base → salt + water.

## Common Compounds & Chemical Names

| Common name | Chemical |
|---|---|
| Common salt | NaCl |
| Baking soda | NaHCO₃ |
| Washing soda | Na₂CO₃·10H₂O |
| Bleaching powder | CaOCl₂ |
| Quicklime | CaO |
| Slaked lime | Ca(OH)₂ |
| Plaster of Paris | CaSO₄·½H₂O |
keyPoints: Air is a mixture; water and CO₂ are compounds; rusting and burning are chemical changes.
Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons; isotopes share atomic number, differ in mass.
Valency = combining capacity; carbon has valency 4.
pH < 7 acidic, 7 neutral, > 7 basic; acid + base → salt + water (neutralisation).
Baking soda = NaHCO₃, washing soda = Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, bleaching powder = CaOCl₂, quicklime = CaO.
Plaster of Paris = CaSO₄·½H₂O; slaked lime = Ca(OH)₂; common salt = NaCl.
items.mnemonic: 'Baking = Bicarbonate' → baking soda is sodium biCARBonate (NaHCO₃).
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9-10 — Matter; Atoms and Molecules; Acids, Bases and Salts

items.title: Chemistry II — Metals, Non-metals, Carbon Compounds & Fertilisers
items.body:
## Metals & Non-metals

- **Metals**: lustrous, malleable, ductile, good conductors; **mercury is the only liquid metal** at room temperature.
- **Non-metals**: generally poor conductors (**graphite is an exception**), brittle.
- **Noble (inert) gases** (He, Ne, Ar, Kr): chemically unreactive; **electric filament bulbs are filled with argon or nitrogen** to stop the tungsten filament from oxidising/burning; helium fills balloons/airships and neon glows in signs.
- **Reactivity series** (high → low): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu > **Ag > Au** (noble/least reactive).

| Alloy | Composition |
|---|---|
| Brass | Copper + Zinc |
| Bronze | Copper + Tin |
| Steel | Iron + Carbon |
| Stainless steel | Iron + Cr + Ni |

## Carbon Compounds

- **Allotropes of carbon**: diamond (hardest natural), graphite (conductor), fullerene, graphene.
- **Hydrocarbons**: methane (CH₄, simplest), ethane, propane, butane (LPG).
- **Polymers**: large chains — natural (cellulose, natural rubber, proteins) vs synthetic (**polythene, PVC, nylon, bakelite**).

## Fertilisers

- **NPK** = Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium.
- **Urea** = major nitrogenous fertiliser; DAP supplies phosphorus; MOP supplies potassium.
keyPoints: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature; non-metals are poor conductors (except graphite).
Electric filament bulbs are filled with argon (or nitrogen), an inert gas, to prevent the filament from oxidising.
Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag > Au; gold and silver are noble metals.
Brass = copper + zinc; bronze = copper + tin; steel = iron + carbon.
Carbon allotropes: diamond, graphite, fullerene, graphene; methane is the simplest hydrocarbon.
Polythene, PVC and nylon are synthetic polymers; cellulose and natural rubber are natural polymers.
Fertilisers supply N-P-K; urea is a nitrogenous fertiliser.
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10 — Metals and Non-metals; Carbon and its Compounds

items.title: Biology — Cell, Human Body, Nutrition & Plant Physiology
items.body:
## The Cell

- **Robert Hooke** first saw 'cells' (cork); **Robert Brown** discovered the nucleus.
- **Mitochondria** = powerhouse of the cell; **ribosomes** = protein synthesis.

| Feature | Plant cell | Animal cell |
|---|---|---|
| Cell wall | Present | Absent |
| Chloroplast | Present | Absent |
| Large vacuole | Present | Small/absent |

## Human Body Systems

- **Digestion** → largest gland is the **liver**; **circulation** → four-chambered heart; **respiration** → gas exchange in **alveoli**.
- **Blood groups**: **O-negative** = universal donor; **AB** = universal recipient.
- **Neuron** = unit of the nervous system; **nephron** = unit of the kidney; **medulla oblongata** controls heartbeat/breathing.

## Nutrition, Vitamins & Hormones

| Deficiency | Disease |
|---|---|
| Vitamin A | Night blindness |
| Vitamin C | Scurvy |
| Vitamin D | Rickets |
| Vitamin B1 | Beriberi |
| Iron | Anaemia |
| Iodine | Goitre |

- Hormones: **insulin** (pancreas → blood sugar), **thyroxine** (thyroid → metabolism), **adrenaline** (fight-or-flight); **pituitary** = master gland (base of brain).

## Plant Physiology & Classification

- **Photosynthesis**: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (light + chlorophyll); **transpiration** = loss of water vapour through stomata.
- **Five-kingdom classification** (Whittaker): Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
keyPoints: Robert Hooke discovered cells (cork); Robert Brown discovered the nucleus; mitochondria = powerhouse.
Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts; animal cells lack both.
Liver is the largest gland; alveoli exchange gases; O-negative = universal donor, AB = universal recipient.
Neuron = nervous system unit; nephron = kidney unit; medulla controls heartbeat and breathing.
Deficiencies: Vitamin A→night blindness, C→scurvy, D→rickets, B1→beriberi, iron→anaemia, iodine→goitre.
Photosynthesis needs chlorophyll and light; Whittaker's five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
items.mnemonic: Five kingdoms 'MPFPA' = Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9-10 — The Fundamental Unit of Life; Life Processes; Control and Coordination; Diversity in Living Organisms
